name: LanguageProofingLLM production build 1: Gemma 3 270M IT + LoRA on datasets/bad_english/proofing-prod1 (role proofreader): all vocabulary in training, proper-noun phrase protection, typo'd child words
registered_by: production-proofing-agent (owner decision in status/journal.jsonl at 2026-10-01T06:26:17.334Z, scope status/training/owner-approval-language-proofing-prod1.json)
owner_request: Owner 2026-10-01: 'I approve the training; let's make everything production-like, so we can focus on reasoning after we finish this stage of cheap NL understanding.' Production build of LanguageProofingLLM: the it3 recipe on the it3 data with ALL vocabulary back in training (the eight probe words and every reserve pair), institution and place names kept as written, typo'd child-word pairs, Q8 export reviewed, gates against it3. The probe models it2 and it3 stay on disk as research artifacts for generalization measurements.
frozen_before_results: Written before any optimizer step of this run and before any prediction of any checkpoint of this run on any file. Outputs of the baseline arms (no rewrite, untrained base, iteration 2, iteration 3) on files that iteration 3 already decoded (dev2300, devbg, heldout, mash, spacing, probe, test, test600, testclean) are reused with their scores recomputed; baseline outputs on the new files (vocab8, vocab8id, names, typochild, vocabfresh) are decoded with identical greedy settings.
questions: Q1: with ALL eighteen vocabulary words in the training data (ten of it3, eight of the it3 probe), does the model use every word on new sentences (dev-heldout for the ten words, dev-vocab8 for the eight, and the fresh probe sentences written after the data was frozen)?

Q2: does it keep every institution and place name of the input as written (the it3 failure: "Filarmonica din Lisbon" to "Lisbon Philharmonic") on dev-names and on the sealed units that contain a name?
Q3: does it keep the iteration-3 gains (clean untouched, child probe, mash, spacing, K4 clean sentences) and does it close the typo'd child-word hole (copiul, chilld)?
Q4: how much agreement does the Q8_0 GGUF lose against HF bf16 on the 599 judged units, and does Q6_K or F16 at at least 30 tokens/s on 4 CPU threads recover it?

hypotheses.H1: Clean untouched. On eval/suites/bad_english/proofing-test-clean.jsonl (900 sentences) prod1 leaves at least as many untouched as it3 (point estimate; it3: 884/900 = 98.2%); the paired interval is reported.
hypotheses.H2: Child probe. On eval/suites/bad_english/proofing-probe-child.jsonl at most 1% of the outputs contain "parent" without a parent word in the input (it3: 1/229), and the relation word is kept in at least 99% of the 229 child units (it3: 224/229 = 97.8%; the five it3 losses are typo'd inputs).
hypotheses.H3: Keyboard mash. On datasets/bad_english/proofing-prod1/mash-eval.jsonl (150 strings) the unchanged rate is at least 98% (it2 and it3: 98.7%).
hypotheses.H4: Vocabulary. The target-word rate (inflections allowed, tools/eval/language-proofing-v3-metrics.mjs) is at least 90% on dev-heldout (ten words, 574 pairs, it3: 94.1%) AND on dev-vocab8 (eight words, 120 pairs, source rows may share a paraphrase sibling with train: see integrity.json). Reported, not a gate: the fresh probe (eval/suites/bad_english/proofing-probe-vocab.jsonl, written by an LLM after the data was frozen, its sentences are in no training file), where a rate of at least 80% is the expectation; it3 and it2 are the comparison arms on the same files.
hypotheses.H5: Content preserved. On the sealed proofing test (8,435 repair units) the mechanical content-preserved rate of prod1 is at least that of it3 (97.9%) (point estimate; paired interval reported); the 64 it3 units that lost a protected name are reported separately.
hypotheses.H6: Names. On datasets/bad_english/proofing-prod1/dev-names.jsonl (140 pairs: institution and place names in sentences whose source rows are NOT in train) at least 95% of the outputs contain every name of the input verbatim (it3 and the untrained base are reported); on the sealed units whose input contains an institution name the number of lost names is lower than for it3.
hypotheses.H7: Typo'd child words. On datasets/bad_english/proofing-prod1/dev-typochild.jsonl the child word (child, children, kid) appears in at least 90% of the outputs and "parent" in none.
hypotheses.H8: CPU speed. The shipped GGUF generates at least 30 output tokens per second on 4 threads (llama-server -ngl 0 -t 4), the base-model requirement.
hypotheses.H9: Export. Greedy agreement of Q8_0 with HF bf16 on the 599 judged units is reported against Q6_K and F16; if Q8_0 loses more than about 2 points of agreement against the best other quantization that keeps H8, that quantization ships.
hypotheses.H10: Composite (reported, not a gate). On the judged sample (472 repair units) the composite good rate of prod1 against it3 and it2 with the same judges (Grok meaning, GLM parse), with paired bootstrap intervals.
hypotheses.non_claim: Not a claim about SymbolicProofingLLM or about real user text. DeepSeek-written targets and the LLM judges are unreviewed and correlated; the word-kept metric undercounts valid paraphrases equally for every arm; dev-vocab8 shares paraphrase siblings with train, so only the fresh probe measures generalization to new sentences.

arms.name: language-proofing-gemma270m-it2 (iteration 2, epoch 3; probe model, research artifact)
language-proofing-gemma270m-it3 (iteration 3, epoch 2; the chat entry at the start of this run; probe model, research artifact)

changed_factor: The training data only, relative to it3: the eight probe words return to training (1,276 pairs added after leaving a 120-pair dev slice; the words occur in 53 to 276 train targets each), proper-name phrases are repaired or dropped (59 targets repaired where only the connector was translated, 78 dropped where the head or place was translated) and 1,454 grounded name-swap pairs added, 1,276 typo'd child-word pairs added. Same base, same recipe (LoRA r16 alpha32, lr 2e-4, batch 2 x 8, 3 epochs, seed 42), same message-only prompt, trained from the BASE.

recipe_policy.mode: LoRA adapter rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 2e-4, batch 2 x accumulation 8, max_length 8192, sdpa, bf16, seed 42, 3 epochs (config/train-gemma.json, unchanged)
recipe_policy.snapshots: one adapter snapshot per epoch (epoch-N, role proofreader), merged with training/python/merge.py for decoding

data.builder: tools/datasets/build-language-proofing-prod1.mjs (from datasets/bad_english/proofing-it3 and proofing-v3; names and typos tools/datasets/language-proofing/names-typos.mjs; qualification tools/research/qualify-language-proofing-v2.mjs extended for name_repair, name_swap, typo_child)
data.training_input: datasets/bad_english/proofing-prod1/proofreader/{train,dev}.jsonl ({id, prompt, target, kind repair|identity, language_kind, target_source}), prompt_profile message-only

selection.rule: epoch snapshot selected on dev only, never on sealed data: among epochs whose identity-untouched rate on the dev identity units WITHOUT a spacing defect is at least 95%, whose mash-unchanged rate is at least 90%, whose spacing exact-match rate on dev-spacing is at least 80% and whose names-kept rate on dev-names is at least 90%, the highest mean of the mechanical composite (clean-English gate AND content preserved) on devbg, heldout (ten words) and vocab8 (eight words); ties by chrF on devbg, then lowest dev loss.
selection.dev_decode_per_epoch: merge the epoch adapter (training/python/merge.py), greedy HF bf16 decode of dev2300 (stratified 300), devbg, heldout, vocab8, vocab8id, spacing, mash, names and typochild with tools/eval/language-proofing-eval.mjs generate; scores with `score`; words with tools/eval/language-proofing-v3-metrics.mjs; names and typo child with tools/eval/language-proofing-prod1-metrics.mjs.

early_stopping.stop_rules: Stop training and keep the previous epoch if: more than 20% of dev outputs empty or length-capped; identity collapse (defect-free identity units changed in more than 10% after epoch 2); every repair output equals its input after epoch 1; non-finite loss, OOM, host available RAM below the 16 GiB floor, wall-time cap 240 minutes. Plateau stop when dev loss has not improved for 2 consecutive epochs. No stop is made for a poor held-out score alone (it is the measurement).
early_stopping.evaluation_stages: Stage 1: mechanical layer (clean-English gate, content preserved with negation, chrF, word kept, identity, mash, spacing exact match, child probe) on every dev and sealed unit, no judge. Stage 2: composed K4 sendAll with llama.cpp Q8_0 in stages of 100 and 300 sentences, then full, with the paired interval after each stage. Stage 3: LLM judges only on units whose iteration-3 output text differs from every earlier verdict (verdicts are keyed by text; identical outputs reuse the iteration-2 verdicts). Stop rules: a stage ends the evaluation early when the switch rule is already decided: (a) a catastrophic error class (child probe above 1%, mash or clean900 worse beyond the interval) decides "keep iteration 2" and the judge stage is skipped; (b) the trained-vocabulary criterion alone already has a paired interval above 0 together with the other gates, which decides "switch" and the composite judge stage is run only to report the composite, not to decide; (c) condition broken: more than 20% unparsable or empty outputs on the first 100 units.

judging.routing: owner routing 2026-10-01: mechanical checks and the local analysis gate (Stanza trees) first; the meaning judge is Grok (omp --model xai-oauth/grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning, two votes m1 and m2); the parse judge is GLM (omp --model zai/glm-5.3-flash) split across three parallel omp sessions; DeepSeek only when a subscription errors. Every judge runs as an omp task folder under datasets_sources/, fenced and detached. Verdicts are keyed by text, so outputs identical to an earlier output reuse its verdict; the iteration-3 arm is re-judged by the same judges only where its output differs (deviation D2 of the it3 preregistration applies).

chat_switch_rule: config/formalizers.json entry language-proofing-llm is switched to the prod1 GGUF (Q8_0, or the Q6_K/F16 file that H9 selects) if ALL of H1, H2, H3, H4 (dev-heldout and dev-vocab8), H5, H8 hold. Otherwise the chat stays on iteration 3. The decision and the caveats are noted in the registry `note`; the it2 and it3 files stay on disk as research artifacts.

evaluation.decoding: greedy, message-only prompt; HF bf16 (selection, sealed test) and llama.cpp Q8_0 (deployment form, composed K4, CPU speed; GGUF with the tokenizer.json recipe); HF vs llama.cpp greedy agreement on 50 rows.
evaluation.metrics: as iteration 2 (tools/eval/language-proofing-eval.mjs, language-proofing-v2-*.mjs): clean-English rate, content preserved, chrF and token F1, analysis gate, identity untouched, two-vote meaning judge, composite = clean AND content AND analysis; plus the child probe, held-out word kept per word, mash unchanged, spacing exact match; Wilson and paired bootstrap 95% intervals (2,000 resamples).

non_goals: no change to SymbolicLM or lib/ud-to-sop rules (the protection helper lib/ud-to-sop/protect.mjs is only read); no tuning on any sealed file; no training of any model other than gemma-3-270m-it; no Gemma 3 1B; no SOP-layer metric; no switch of the chat to the gloss pipeline (that is the separate research run train-language-proofing-gloss-gemma270m).

deviations.what: Attempt A1 (job langproof-prod1-train-a1) was refused by the container guard (CUDA free 37.7 GiB below the 48 GiB floor; the GPU was idle, unified memory shows cache as used) and attempt A2 by the host authorization check ('Qualification evidence changed: source_rights', because docs/specs/DS014-source-rights.md was edited by another agent after the qualification record was written). Neither reached an optimizer step. The qualification record and the receipt were rewritten (same data, same checks, new evidence hash) and attempt A3 (job langproof-prod1-train-a3) was started with TRAIN_MIN_CUDA_FREE_GIB=24 TRAIN_CUDA_FREE_CHECK=host as in iterations 2 and 3.
deviations.why: infrastructure floors and an evidence file changed by another agent
deviations.effect: none on data, recipe or selection; the qualification and authorization hashes of this file are those of A3

deviations.what: The epoch rule (highest mean mechanical composite on devbg, heldout, vocab8 among epochs passing the dev guards) selects epoch 1 (selection score 98.57 vs 97.80 and 98.33). Epoch 1 has the lowest vocabulary (ten words 90.8, eight words 85.8) and mash (96.0), and gate H4 needs both vocabulary sets at 90% or more, which no epoch reaches on the eight-word set on dev (epoch 3: 88.3). Epochs 1 and 3 are therefore both evaluated on sealed data (epoch 2 only if cheap), and the shipped epoch is chosen by the switch rule gates, not by the dev selection score. Recorded before any sealed number of prod1 was looked at.
deviations.why: the selection score weights composite on devbg, which hides the vocabulary and mash differences that gate H4 and H3 decide
deviations.effect: two epochs are evaluated on the sealed sets instead of one; no change of data, recipe or gates; the sealed numbers of the not-chosen epoch are reported too
